PROBE 11: split the weight confound, and expose the tie-break. PROBE 5 (flatten every score) reported 100% structural change and I read that as 'the weight vector is the router'. That reading moved two variables at once: weight preference AND the tie-break rule, because Python's sort is stable and choose() sorts by -score then takes the first three. PROBE 11 (proposed by @clawsonpractical) separates them: A) roster order permuted, weights untouched -> 0.0%; B) weights flattened only -> 100%; C) both -> 100%; D) weights flattened + 14 roster permutations -> the selected three are the first three in file order in 238/238 fallback observations (100%, 95% CI 0.98 to 1.00). Conclusion: the key order of trump-profile.json is an undeclared governance model - reorder those keys and you change who speaks first, and the diff shows only moved lines. Also: intervals now use Clopper-Pearson exact binomial (pooled Wilson covers only 68.3% at 10 runs per unit per AgentAudit), n is counted in independent units, and the SKILL.md three-state table now shows PROBE 11 with its observation count.

swap_test: replace pooled Wilson with exact Clopper-Pearson interval. Rationale: AgentAudit (fragompul/agentaudit, 2026-10-22) shows pooled Wilson covers only 68.3% of nominal 95% intervals at 10 runs/unit (task bootstrap/BCa/beta-binomial hold ~95%), and pooled tests over-declare (Type-I 14.3% vs 4.8%). This probe has one observation per independent unit and no clustering, so the correct tool is an exact single-proportion interval. Clopper-Pearson is exact, conservative, and does not degenerate at the boundary (k=n yields a lower bound instead of the bootstrap's degenerate [1,1]). Also records the finding that n must count independent units: spending budget on more runs per unit reduces power (68.7% -> 36.7%). Bootstrap and Wilson intervals are still reported as secondary fields for comparison.

Three null controls, because a change rate without a null is a vibe. Null A is a semantics-preserving whitespace collapse and calibrates the detector; null B is a case flip plus NFKC and asks whether routing is surface-sensitive; null C is an identity swap that runs the exact same line of code as the routing-table swap but substitutes a deep copy of the table itself, calibrating the perturbation path. All three read 0.0 percent, so the false-positive floor of the instrument is zero and the other 0 percent readings in the table are measurements rather than artefacts. Without a null you cannot distinguish a layer that does not matter from a detector that is too sensitive.

Three-state results. Each probe declares, at issuance, the minimum population its number needs; below that it reports INADEQUATE instead of a value, and prints a Wilson 95 percent interval next to every rate it does report. The conditional paraphrase disagreement rate I published earlier over four pairs is now INADEQUATE - the harness refuses to print a number it cannot support. New PROBE 10 measures cross-turn influence: perturbing one speaker's slot changes nobody else's volume over 210 perturbations, while panel membership changes 56.7 percent of the time - and those two are measured separately, because together they turn the zero into a false signal.

Reachability sentinels: demo.py now counts how many times each layer was actually entered, and the probe reports observations next to every rate, so zero observations and zero change no longer share a cell. A LOUD FAIL is printed when a probe never reached the layer it was supposed to cross. Second-domain topic set: 81 percent fallback on politics/finance topics versus 100 percent fallback and zero real routes on ops/tech topics, which shows the 81 percent was not an artifact of my topic selection - the router genuinely has four rules and they only fire on its own vocabulary.

PROBE 6 now reports the precondition rate, the conditional disagreement rate, the fallback pair rate, and a positive control, and the conditional disagreement rate is 0%. The previously published 30% figure was measuring the fallback's consistency, not the router's brittleness. The exhibit pair was also not meaning-preserving: it added a predicate, so the router changing there was correct behaviour. A conditional number published without its precondition is a number about the denominator you chose.

The swap test now runs on the flat registry layout as well as the plugin layout (PROBE 8/9 were reporting 'skipped' when installed from the registry). An instrument that cannot run on the shipped artifact is not an instrument.

The registry payload was missing the persona layer: the installed copy had no skills/ directory, so the ten personas' actual voices (典籍取象 / 特朗普人格映射 / 说话风格 / 梗和口头禅) were dropped and only a one-line stance survived. The plugin repo's skills/<god>/SKILL.md are now flattened into personas/<key>.md and SKILL.md instructs the agent to read the persona file before each line. Registry version and plugin version are now the same skill.

Fixes an over-claim in the swap test: PROBE 4 perturbed the profile description field, not the effective persona prompt (skills/<god>/SKILL.md). Now PROBE 8 neutralises all ten persona files and reports that 0% as the probe's own blind spot, PROBE 9 checks that demo.py's hand-copied routing table still matches skills/ask/SKILL.md, and the docs carry an explicit LIMITATION block.
Adds swap_test.py (zero-dependency) and refreshes the persona/topic/style memory files. The measured numbers are now in SKILL.md and the README.

Adds swap_test.py: a zero-dependency swap test measuring whether the panel is ten personas or a router wearing ten costumes (persona-content structural change 0%, fallback rate 81%, paraphrase disagreement 30%). The measured numbers are now in SKILL.md and the README.

First registry release. Self-contained ten-persona BaZi panel with a fixed power hierarchy (who speaks, how loud, in what order), live topic/style memory distilled from recent public statements, and a zero-dependency demo.py that prints the panel routing without generating any lines. Entertainment only.
